ai.literal: I will hide, alas, I, this pain! To those who draw out, spring water like, it increases.
ai.translation: I try to hide this pain, but alas! Like a spring that swells the more water is drawn from it, my sorrow only increases.
ai.modern: நான் இந்தத் துன்பத்தை மறைக்கவே முயல்கிறேன்; ஆனால், நீரை இறைக்க இறைக்கப் பெருகும் ஊற்றுநீரைப் போல, இந்த நோய் நான் மறைக்க முயல முயல அதிகமாகிறது.
ai.explanation: The speaker is suffering from the pain of separation and tries to conceal it from others. However, the effort to suppress the sorrow only makes it grow stronger. The couplet uses a vivid simile: 'ஊற்றுநீர்' (spring water) which flows more abundantly the more it is drawn out ('இறைப்பவர்க்கு'). The particle 'மன்' expresses the speaker's frustration at the impossibility of hiding the pain. The word 'நோய்' here specifically refers to the lovesickness or grief of separation.

ai.literal: Hiding even I am unable; this pain, to the one who caused the pain, telling even gives shame.
ai.translation: I cannot bear to hide this pain. Yet, telling of it to the one who caused it brings me shame.
ai.modern: இந்தத் துன்பத்தை என்னால் மறைத்து வைக்கவும் முடியவில்லை. இதை எனக்குத் தந்தவரிடமே சொல்வதற்கும் எனக்கு வெட்கமாக இருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The speaker is caught in a painful dilemma regarding her lovesickness. She is unable to conceal the intense suffering she feels inside. At the same time, her natural modesty prevents her from openly declaring her pain to her lover, who is the very cause of it. The repetition of the word 'நோய்' (pain or disease) emphasizes the inescapable nature of her affliction.

ai.literal: Desire and modesty, life as a carrying pole, hang [in] my unable-to-bear body's inside.
ai.translation: Desire and modesty hang balanced on the carrying-pole of my life, within my frail, unenduring body.
ai.modern: காமமும் நாணமும் எனது உயிரையே காவடியாகக் கொண்டு, தாங்கும் வலிமையற்ற எனது உடம்பின் உள்ளே இரு முனைகளிலும் தொங்குகின்றன.
ai.explanation: The speaker describes her internal struggle using the vivid metaphor of a carrying pole (kāvaṭi). Her fragile life acts as the pole resting within her frail body, which can barely endure the emotional strain. On either end of this pole hang her intense desire and her natural modesty, perfectly balanced but weighing heavily upon her.

ai.literal: Desire's sea indeed exists; that crossing safe raft indeed is not.
ai.translation: There is indeed a vast sea of desire, but there is no safe raft to cross it.
ai.modern: காமமாகிய கடல் இருக்கவே செய்கிறது, ஆனால் அதைக் கடந்து செல்வதற்கான பாதுகாப்பான தெப்பம் மட்டும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The speaker compares their overwhelming desire to a vast, uncrossable sea. While this ocean of passion is very real and present, there is no safe raft available to navigate it. This highlights the helplessness and isolation felt when consumed by intense longing without any means of relief.

ai.literal: If in enmity what will they become, I wonder, sorrow's coming within friendship those who cause.
ai.translation: If he brings me such sorrow even while we are in love, what would he do if he became my enemy?
ai.modern: அன்பாக இருக்கும்போதே எனக்குத் துன்பம் தருபவர், ஒருவேளை பகையானால் என்ன செய்வாரோ?
ai.explanation: The speaker laments the pain caused by her lover's departure. She wonders how much more she would suffer if he were actually her enemy, since he causes her so much grief even while they are in love. The contrast between friendship and enmity highlights the unbearable nature of her current sorrow.

ai.literal: Joy (is) a sea, but love, when that afflicts, sorrow (is) bigger than that.
ai.translation: The joy of love is as vast as the sea. But when it afflicts, the sorrow is even greater than the sea.
ai.modern: காமத்தால் வரும் இன்பம் கடல் அளவு பெரியது; ஆனால் அது துன்புறுத்தும்போது வரும் துன்பம் கடலை விடப் பெரியது.
ai.explanation: The speaker compares the joy of love to the vastness of the sea. However, when love brings separation and longing, the resulting sorrow is even greater than the sea itself. The word 'அடுங்கால்' (when it afflicts) highlights the intense pain of unfulfilled desire. Thus, the couplet contrasts the immense pleasure of love with its even more overwhelming pain.

ai.literal: Desire's fierce flood having swum, shore I see not; at midnight even, I alone exist.
ai.translation: I swim the fierce flood of desire but can see no shore. Even at midnight, I alone remain awake.
ai.modern: காமமாகிய கடுமையான வெள்ளத்தில் நீந்தியும் நான் கரையைச் சேரவில்லை; நள்ளிரவிலும் நான் மட்டுமே உறங்காமல் விழித்திருக்கிறேன்.
ai.explanation: The speaker compares her intense longing to a fierce, endless flood that she struggles to swim across without ever finding the shore. While the rest of the world sleeps peacefully, she alone remains awake, trapped in her suffering. The contrast between the vast, turbulent flood of desire and the stillness of midnight highlights her profound isolation.

ai.literal: Enduring life all having put to sleep having been gracious night, me except is not companion.
ai.translation: The night has graciously put all living beings to sleep; now it has no companion except me.
ai.modern: உலகத்து உயிர்களை எல்லாம் தூங்கச் செய்துவிட்டுத் தனித்திருக்கும் இந்த இரவுக்கு, இப்போது என்னைத் தவிர வேறு துணை இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The speaker, suffering from the pain of separation, observes the deep stillness of the night. The word 'tuyiṟṟi' means making others sleep, and 'aḷittu' shows the night's kindness in giving rest to all creatures. Since everyone else is asleep, the speaker feels that the night itself is awake and lonely, with no one but her for company. This highlights her own sleeplessness and profound isolation.

ai.literal: Cruel person / than cruelty / themselves / cruel / these days / long / passing / nights
ai.translation: The long, dragging nights of these days are themselves more cruel than the cruelty of the cruel one.
ai.modern: கொடியவரான காதலரின் கொடுமையை விட, இப்போது நீண்டுகொண்டே போகும் இந்த இரவுகள் மிகவும் கொடியவையாக இருக்கின்றன.
ai.explanation: The speaker laments the unbearable length of the nights while separated from her lover. She calls her lover cruel for leaving her alone to suffer. However, she feels that the nights that drag on endlessly these days are even more cruel than his abandonment. The repetition of the word cruel emphasizes how the agonizingly slow passage of time in the dark multiplies her sorrow.

words.gloss: to the place where he is

ai.literal: Mind resembling, to the place where he is, if able to go, flood water, swim-not-they alas, my eyes.
ai.translation: If my eyes could travel to where my lover is, just as my mind does, they would not be swimming in this flood of tears.
ai.modern: என் மனத்தைப் போல என் கண்களும் அவர் உள்ள இடத்திற்குச் செல்ல முடியுமானால், அவை இப்படி வெள்ளம் போன்ற கண்ணீரில் நீந்திக் கொண்டிருக்க மாட்டா.
ai.explanation: The heroine laments her physical separation from her lover while her mind is already with him. She wishes her eyes had the same ability as her mind to instantly travel to where he is. If they could, they would be looking at him instead of swimming in a flood of tears. The contrast between the swift, unbound mind and the physically bound, weeping eyes highlights her deep sorrow.
